```{python}
#| label: fig-nand2-schematic
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Transistor-level schematic of a NAND2 standard cell: two parallel PMOS pull-up transistors and two stacked NMOS pull-down transistors. Different drive strengths of the cell simply scale the transistor widths."

import schemdraw as sd
import schemdraw.elements as elm

sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=2, fontsize=10)

    # supply rail
    d += elm.Vdd().at((2, 8)).label('$V_\\mathrm{DD}$')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((2, 8), (2, 7.6))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0.5, 7.6), (4.5, 7.6))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 7.6))

    # parallel PMOS
    p1 = elm.PFet(bulk=False).at((0.5, 7.6)).anchor('source').theta(0).reverse()
    d += p1
    p2 = elm.PFet(bulk=False).at((4.5, 7.6)).anchor('source').theta(0)
    d += p2

    # output node
    d += elm.Line().at(p1.drain).to((0.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Line().at(p2.drain).to((4.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0.5, 4.5), (4.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 4.5))

    # NMOS stack
    n1 = elm.NFet(bulk=False).at((2, 4.5)).anchor('drain').theta(0).reverse()
    d += n1
    n2 = elm.NFet(bulk=False).at(n1.source).anchor('drain').theta(0)
    d += n2
    d += elm.Ground().at(n2.source)

    # inputs
    d += elm.Line().at(p1.gate).to((-1.6, p1.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().at(n1.gate).to((-1.6, n1.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((-1.6, p1.gate[1]), (-1.6, n1.gate[1]))
    ya = (p1.gate[1] + n1.gate[1]) / 2
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((-1.6, ya), (-2.4, ya))
    d += elm.Dot().at((-1.6, ya))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((-2.4, ya)).label('A', 'left')

    d += elm.Line().at(p2.gate).to((7.2, p2.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().at(n2.gate).to((7.2, n2.gate[1]))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((7.2, p2.gate[1]), (7.2, n2.gate[1]))
    yb = (p2.gate[1] + n2.gate[1]) / 2
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((7.2, yb), (8.0, yb))
    d += elm.Dot().at((7.2, yb))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((8.0, yb)).label('B', 'right')

    # output
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((4.5, 4.5), (5.9, 4.5))
    d += elm.Dot().at((4.5, 4.5))
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((5.9, 4.5)).label('Y', 'right')
```
